events.text: At {wd_inn} three tether-cutters from the low isles have the keeper pinned against the kettle-shelf over a mooring fee they mean never to pay. The guests study their cups. The keeper, a stooped woman with tea-stained sleeves, looks straight at you, the only stranger who has just docked.

effects.log: You stand. The cutters count your hands and your eyes and decide the fee can be paid after all. The keeper sends you the best pot in the house.
You do not ask them to stop. The shelf needs mending, the cutters need a long float home, and every landing on the route will hear of it.

choices.text: Keep your eyes on your cup

effects.log: It is not your landing and not your fight. The cutters leave unpaid, and the keeper does not look at you again.

events.text: A freight-kite has snapped a line in the yard of {wd_inn}. A crate of lantern-oil swings over the edge of the landing, and a porter's child hangs in the rope net beneath it. The yard is full of travellers. None of them moves.

effects.log: You set your shoulders to the rope and heave. The child scrambles up the net. The porter cannot stop thanking you, and the whole house stands you supper.
You make eight travellers take the line together. It works. They are all a little proud afterwards, and so are you.
Someone else hauls eventually. You are already back on the bridge.

events.text: The cutters bullying the keeper of {wd_inn} take one look at you and go very quiet. Your realm sits on the room like pressure before a storm, and even low-isle thieves can feel it. The leader sets the fee on the counter with both hands.

choices.text: Let them go with a warning

effects.log: They go, bowing. The keeper pours you tea with shaking hands and refuses your thanks.
You make an example. The routes will talk of it for a month, and so will the low isles.

events.text: A silk-sleeved broker at {wd_inn} is lashing a serving boy with words for spilling cloud-tea on a ledger. The room has gone quiet. The broker sees your look, laughs, and says something about knowing one's place on the isles.

choices.text: Send the ledger over the rail

effects.log: A gust takes the ledger off the landing. The broker chases it down the stairs, and the serving boy brings you tea the rest of the night.

choices.text: Dry the ledger with a pass of your palm

effects.log: The page is dry in a heartbeat. The scolding stops, if only because the broker is confused.
The broker pours you a cup. It tastes of nothing.

events.text: {npc} sits down across from you at {wd_inn} without asking, because every other table is full, and orders two bowls of mist-rice instead of one. "You look like someone with a long drift behind you," {he} says. "So do I. Eat."

mem.note: shared a table and a long night of stories

effects.log: By the second pot you have each told the other things you have told nobody. {npc} laughs like a shutter banging open.
{npc} does not mind. At dawn {he} pays for both bowls and is gone, leaving a note: "Same wind, maybe."
{npc} shrugs and takes the rice to the stairs.

events.text: Fog pins everyone indoors at {wd_inn} for three days, and on the second you and {npc}, a traveller with a worn zither-case, start a game of stone-and-cloud by the stove. By the third day the whole house is watching, and neither of you has taken a game.

effects.log: {npc} knows you let {him} win, and likes you better for it.

mem.note: lost a good game to you

effects.log: You win by a single stone. {npc} stares at the board, then laughs and demands another.

events.text: {npc} looks up when you come into {wd_inn}, and stares. "My teacher's teacher told stories about {wd_past_title}," {he} says. "You walk the way the stories say. Forgive me. Sit, please. I am buying." Your soul hears the old name and turns over in its sleep.

effects.log: The stories are wrong in every detail and right in every way that matters. {npc} tells them with shining eyes.

choices.text: Say you have never heard the name

effects.log: {npc} looks disappointed, then sly. "Of course not," {he} says, and buys you a bowl anyway.

events.text: {npc}, a skinny young drifter with a bamboo stick for a sword, has been watching you eat at {wd_inn} for an hour. At last {he} comes over and kneels on the planks. "Teach me," {he} says. "Or let me carry your pack. I do not care which. I only want to go where the wind takes you."

effects.log: You tell {npc} to get up off the planks. {He} follows you onto the bridge, grinning.

choices.text: Give advice and a charm for the road

mem.note: was given advice and a charm

effects.log: You tell {npc} which landings keep honest teachers and press a small wind-charm into {his} hand.
"Go home," you say. {npc} goes, slowly, looking back over a shoulder.

events.text: {npc} is sweeping the landing of {wd_inn} for a bowl of rice, and has been watching you since you came in. When you stand to go, {he} drops the broom. "I have heard of your faction," {he} says. "Everyone on these routes has. Is it true it takes anyone who will work?"

effects.log: You bring {npc} home. The gate guards look at the broom-callused hands and nod.

choices.text: Tell {him} the truth about the work

effects.log: You tell {npc} how hard it is. {He} listens to every word and is still there in the morning.

mem.note: was told there was no room

effects.log: {npc} picks the broom back up.

events.text: Two young drifters are quarrelling over the last dumpling at {wd_inn}, and the smaller one, {npc}, is winning, which is interesting. When it is over, {npc} gives the dumpling back to the bigger one. You watch {him} do it, and think of your own gate, and your own halls with room in them.

choices.text: Offer {npc} a place at your gate

mem.note: was offered a place at your gate

effects.log: {npc} stares, then bows so low {his} forehead hits the table. You have a new disciple, found on the road.
You order a basket of dumplings. Both drifters remember you for years.

events.text: A wandering lutanist is not who you notice at {wd_inn}; {npc} is, humming off-key over a cooling pot, and the hum stops dead the moment {he} sees you grinning. {He} marches over and sets the pot down. "Well? Is it the tune that is funny, or the one humming it?"

mem.note: talked until the lamps burned low

effects.log: "Then you have no taste," {npc} says, sitting down, "and I like you anyway." You talk until the lamps burn low.
{npc} looks at you a long moment, then laughs. "Good answer," {he} says.
{npc} shrugs, and starts another song.

events.text: The only seat left at {wd_inn} is beside {npc}, who has a sky-chart spread over half the table and is arguing with it. "This current does not exist," {npc} says to you, as if you had been sitting there for hours. "I have flown it twice."

effects.log: You redraw the current together on the back of the menu board. {npc} keeps the board.
You trade winds until midnight. {npc} has flown farther than you, and listened better.

events.text: {npc} kicks your stool as {he} passes it at {wd_inn}, and does not apologise. "Nice blade," {he} says. "Shame about who is hanging it." The room goes quiet, waiting to see what kind of traveller you are.

effects.log: You laugh. It is the last thing {npc} expected, and {he} does not know what to do with it. {He} will remember that.

mem.note: was shamed in front of the teahouse

effects.log: The stool catches {npc} behind the knees. The room laughs. {npc} gets up red in the face and swears this is not over.

mem.note: gave you a name to remember

effects.log: "{npc}," {he} says. "Remember it." You will, as it turns out.

events.text: At {wd_inn} {npc} has beaten every guest at thumb-wrestling over the tea-tray and is looking for someone new. {His} eyes find you. {He} sets an elbow on your table and smiles with too many teeth.

effects.log: It goes on a long time. You win, barely, and {npc} looks at you as if you had stolen something.
{npc} tells the room you are afraid. Let {him}.

events.text: A blind storyteller at {wd_inn} tells of a sword immortal who crossed the Sea of Clouds on a single willow leaf without once touching an isle. The guests argue over whether it is true. The storyteller only smiles and holds out a bowl.

choices.text: Put a spirit-chip in the bowl

effects.log: The storyteller tells you, privately, that the leaf was a ferry and the immortal sat very still.

choices.text: Tell a tale of your own

effects.log: Your tale is shorter and duller, but the room is kind. The storyteller nods as if you had paid.

events.text: The keeper of {wd_inn} has a lintel of names: every traveller who sheltered a season has carved one into the beam over the door. Some are so old that the wood has grown over them. The keeper hands you the knife.

effects.log: You carve it small, in a corner, between two names you do not know. It looks as if it has always been there.
You read them all. One of them makes you stop, for no reason you can name.

events.text: On the lintel over the door of {wd_inn}, among the names of old travellers, someone long ago carved "{wd_past_title}". The keeper notices you staring. "A legend of these routes," the keeper says. "They say the one who carved it will come back one day and settle the tab."

effects.log: You settle a tab two lifetimes old. The keeper laughs, then stops laughing, and takes the payment very carefully.

choices.text: Run your thumb over the name

effects.log: The cuts fit your hand. Something in you settles, like a traveller setting down a pack.

events.text: The champion of {wd_inn} is a vast cheerful kite-ferryman who has never been beaten at the cloud-dumplings, and by the twelfth bowl the whole house is standing on the benches. By the twentieth the ferryman is asleep on the floor and you are still upright, more or less, and the room is chanting.

choices.text: Raise your teacup to the ferryman

effects.log: You toast the fallen champion. When the ferryman wakes, the first thing said is a laughing demand for a rematch next season.
You walk out in a perfect straight line, and then sit down very carefully in the yard where nobody can see, and loosen your belt.

events.text: You remember the fourteenth bowl. After the fifteenth you lie down, only for a moment. You wake in the kite-shed of {wd_inn} with a pack-goat staring at you and the house champion snoring in the next stall, and someone has drawn a moustache on your face in lamp-soot. You suspect the champion.

effects.log: The house laughs with you, not at you, by the time you come back in. Mostly.
Fair is fair. The champion wakes, sees, and roars with laughter.

events.text: {npc} slams the bowl down across the table from you at {wd_inn}. "Again," {he} says, for the twentieth time. This time {his} chopsticks miss the dumpling. {npc} sits back, looks at the rafters, and slides gently under the table, still glaring.

mem.note: was helped up from under the table

effects.log: {npc} lets you, and hates it, and does not hate you quite as much as before.
The house steps over {npc} all evening. {He} will remember every step.

events.text: "Under the table," {npc} says, very pleased, "is where you belong." You would argue, but you are under the table, too full to move, and the planks of {wd_inn} are swaying gently with the wind, and {npc} is eating one more dumpling just to show it can be done.

effects.log: "Next season," you say to the planks. {npc} laughs. It is almost friendly.
You swear it from the floor. {npc} eats to it.

events.text: The travelling flautist at {wd_inn} plays first, a fast bright wind-tune, and the room claps. Then you play, something slow that you did not know you remembered. When you stop, nobody claps for a moment. Then the flautist lowers the flute and bows to you.

effects.log: You bow to each other. The flautist teaches you a new tune as payment for the old one.
The two of you play until the fog lifts. The keeper gives you both free beds.

events.text: The flautist at {wd_inn} plays like water falling off a cliff, and you play like someone carrying it back up. The room is polite about it, which is worse. Afterwards the flautist sits with you and shows you, kindly, where your fingers went wrong.

effects.log: You learn more in an hour of losing than in a year of practice.

choices.text: Ask for a rematch next season

effects.log: "Gladly," the flautist says. "Practise the third bar."

events.text: {npc} steps up before you can, a flute held like a drawn blade, and plays a hard, glittering run at {wd_inn} while watching your hands. You do not match it. You answer with one long low note, and the room leans toward you, and {npc} lowers the flute with a thin, furious smile.

effects.log: You play a duet. {npc} plays it beautifully, and pretends not to have enjoyed it.

mem.note: lost the duel before a crowd

effects.log: You take the applause. {npc} takes the door.

events.text: At {wd_inn} the applause is for {npc}, and you are the first to clap, because it was the better tune and you heard it in the first bars. {npc} comes over, pink with pride. "Second place suits you," {he} says. "Come back when you are hungry."

effects.log: {npc} looks startled, and then nods once.
You practise all night in the kite-shed. {npc} hears it, and smiles in the dark.

events.text: You and {npc} take a jar, three sticks of incense and a wind-bell from a stall, and climb the crag behind the landing at sunset. Three bows to the sky, three to the sea of clouds. "Not born on the same day," {npc} says, "but on the same wind." You say the rest of it together.

choices.text: Cut your palms and share the cup

mem.note: shared the cup of the oath

effects.log: A small cut, a shared cup. {npc} grins at you over the rim like someone who has finally come home.
"Whatever comes," you say. "Whatever comes," {npc} says back. It is enough.

events.text: {npc} kneels beside you on the crag and stops before the first bow. "They say you have done things," {he} says. "Hard things. I do not care. I am not swearing to the stories. I am swearing to you." Then {he} bows.

mem.note: swore to you, not the stories

effects.log: You bow together, three and three. Whatever you are, you are no longer alone in the wind.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the worst of it first

mem.note: heard the worst of you and swore anyway

effects.log: You tell {npc} the worst. {He} listens, and bows anyway.

events.text: {npc}, your sworn sibling, drifts into the landing with a torn sleeve and three bounty-kites a day behind. "I would not ask," {npc} says, "but you would never forgive me if I did not."

effects.log: You meet the kites at the bridge-end, together. They decide the bounty is not worth it.

choices.text: Hide {npc} and send the kites astray

effects.log: You send the kites three isles the wrong way. {npc} sleeps in your loft and laughs about it for years.
You close the shutter. {npc} stands outside a long while before going. The routes will hear of this.

events.text: A jade slip in {npc}'s untidy hand: "I am marrying at the new moon. You are the only kin I have. If you are not there I will hold the feast open until you come, and everyone will be very annoyed with you."

choices.text: Fly all night to get there

effects.log: You arrive at dawn, windblown and late. {npc} throws both arms around you in front of the whole feast.

choices.text: Send a gift and your regrets

effects.log: The gift arrives. {npc} writes back a short, polite slip. It is the politeness that stings.

events.text: {npc}, your sworn sibling, finds you at a mooring-post with a jar of good cloud-wine and no reason at all. "The anniversary," {npc} says. "Of the crag. Or near enough. I lost count." You sit by the rail until the stars come out, and talk about nothing and everything.

choices.text: Raise a cup to the oath

effects.log: You raise your cup to the crag, and to the wind, and to whoever is still to come.
You hear everything, the good years and the bad. {npc} has been waiting to tell someone.

events.text: You lay {wd_sworn} to rest on the crag behind a waystation, because that is where the oath was sworn and where {wd_sworn} would have laughed to be remembered. You pour a cup for the clouds and one for the sea beneath. The wind is very quiet.

choices.text: Carve the oath on the stone

effects.log: You carve the words you said together. Travellers stop to read them for years.
You drift on, because that is what the wind is for. You leave the cup on the stone.

events.text: {npc} is waiting on the rope-bridge with a drawn blade. "Every teahouse on these routes tells your stories now," {he} says. "I am sick of them. Today the story ends."

ok.log: You beat {npc} on the swaying planks, and help {him} up afterwards. {He} does not thank you.

fail.log: {npc} beats you on the swaying planks and walks away without a word, which is somehow worse.

effects.log: {npc} stares at you. Then, slowly, {he} lowers the blade. "One meal," {he} says. It turns into a long night, and a friendship.

events.text: {npc} sends a jade slip instead of a challenge this time. "I am tired of hating you," it says. "It takes too much effort and the stories keep getting better for you. Meet me at the teahouse. I will pay."

effects.log: {npc} pays, as promised, and grumbles about it all night. By morning you are friends, more or less.

choices.text: Write back that you are busy

effects.log: {npc} reads the reply and tears it into very small pieces.

events.text: {npc}, whom you met at a teahouse and have not been able to stop thinking about, drifts up to your mooring with two bowls of noodles and no excuse at all. "I was passing," {he} says. You live nowhere near anywhere.

effects.log: {npc} stays the season. By the end of it neither of you pretends it was a coincidence.
You eat together as friends. {npc} is a good friend. The look {he} gives you at the rail says {he} hoped for more.

events.text: A jade slip comes from {npc}, whom you met in the drifting isles: three pages about currents and teahouses and a goat {he} met, and at the very end, one line. "I keep wishing you were there to see it."

effects.log: You fly for a week. {npc} is standing on the landing when you arrive, as if {he} knew.
You write back about your own currents. The slips go on for years, warm and careful.

events.text: A storyteller on a drifting landing tells of {wd_title}, who out-drank a ferryman, a champion and a sworn rival in a single season of fog and never once dropped a blade. You sit at the back. Nobody knows you. The tale is wildly wrong, and you are, it seems, a legend.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the wind laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: A porter hums your tune on a rope-bridge between isles you have never crossed. The tune came from a pedlar, who had it from {wd_title}, who could, the pedlar swore, quiet a thunderhead with three notes.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the wind laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: At a waystation far from anywhere, a young traveller asks the keeper to point out {wd_title}. "The one whose sworn kin would cross a sea of clouds for a slip of jade," the traveller says. The keeper points at you.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the wind laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: The children of a landing-village have a new game: one plays the tether-cutter, one the keeper, and one, always the smallest, plays {wd_title}, who comes in out of the fog and sets things right.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the wind laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: Teahouse keepers on three routes have started bolting their tables to the floor. Nobody says why. Everybody knows why. They are waiting for {wd_title}.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the wind laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: A pedlar looks at your boots and your face and laughs. "I know you," the pedlar says. "Every landing from the western lights to the eastern fog knows you. {wd_title}, they call you. Is there an isle you have not touched?"

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the wind laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.
